candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, Appendix A, printed p.22 / PDF p.26, 'Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement)': define performance improvement/quality assurance activities; participate in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes; utilize research/references for performance-improvement actions; evaluate impact of performance-improvement measures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement)
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret a process-of-care quality measure as an assessment of whether recommended care processes are being delivered according to applicable evidence-based guidelines, standards, or practice parameters.

options.A: Whether recommended steps in care are being provided according to applicable guidelines, standards, or practice parameters
options.B: Only the hospital's research productivity, without measuring care delivery
options.C: Whether bedside clinical judgment can be replaced by a standardized measure
options.D: Only the hospital's financial performance, without evaluating healthcare processes

candidate.rationale: CMS describes process-of-care measures as measures focused on steps that should be followed to provide good care and whether recommended care is delivered based on guidelines, standards of care, or practice parameters. CMS uses quality measures for quality improvement, public reporting, and other quality programs. Therefore A is correct. B and D misstate what is being measured, and C incorrectly treats measurement as a substitute for individualized clinical judgment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CMS process-of-care measures assess whether recommended steps in care are delivered according to guidelines, standards, or practice parameters and are used within quality-improvement and reporting activities.
